newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand managed to hold below the 4.50 level on Thursday afternoon after being pressured by importer demand for dollars, dealers said.
At 1416 GMT the rand was quoted at 4.4970/5020 on the dollar from 4.4830/4860 late on Wednesday.
"There was quite a bit of importer demand which briefly pushed the rand over the 4.50 level in the early afternoon where it was met by some offers," one currency trader said.
"We're currently in a consolidation phase which could take the rand up to the 4.5160 to 4.5250 levels over the next couple of days before renewed bullishness sets in," he added.

The unit started its weaker drift shortly after the official opening on the back of local demand for dollars which was stemmed by smaller banks showing offers on the upside, dealers said. Volumes had been thin, they added.
"The 4.50 level is the important one and we will be waiting to see whether it holds ahead of the week-end," a trader said.

The market was nervous ahead of the release of South Africa's gold and foreign exchange reserves, due out on Friday, traders said. Reserves are seen falling to 10.1 billion rand in August from 10.37 billion in July, according to a consensus forecast of economists polled by Reuters.
Against the crosses, the rand was trading at 7.0469/0561 on sterling from 7.0212/0312 and at 0.3298/3302 marks from 0.3302/3307 marks previously.

Long bond yields tracked the rand higher and were also hampered by lower U.S. Treasuries on the back of the release of lower-than-expected U.S. jobless claims on Thursday, re-awakening fears of a Federal Reserve rate hike in September.
The 30-year T-bond was last trading at a 7.12 percent yield, close to the week's high, from 7.10 percent overnight.

"It's been another relatively quiet day... the focus is still on the release of U.S. payrolls and local reserves on Friday. There was a bit of squaring of positions and some institutional nibbling at the higher levels (above 15.40 percent) but the market is directionless," a dealer noted.
At 1416 GMT the benchmark R150 stock was trading at 15.43 percent from 15.33 percent late on Wednesday, while the E168 was at 15.56 percent from 15.48 percent overnight.
Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net buyers of 62.67 million rand of South African bonds on Wednesday after buying 32.28 million rand of bonds on Tuesday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 3.73 billion rand on Wednesday after 4.66 billion rand on Tuesday.
On the money market, three-month NCDs were unchanged at between 15.90 to 16.05 percent, while 90-day BAs were also steady at between 15.30 to 15.50 percent.
The Reserve Bank put the money market shortage at 8.532 billion rand on Wednesday from 8.551 billion rand on Tuesday.
